replies.user: [CURRICULUM: Unit 1, Lesson 1] Teach me what physically happens inside an LLM when I type a prompt. Start with tokenization and next-token prediction. After explaining, give me a hands-on exercise.
replies.raw:
Here's something that might surprise you: the word "bank" is always the same token — whether you're talking about a riverbank or a savings account.

The AI has no idea which one you mean just from that word alone.

So how does it figure it out?

---

**Tokenization** is the very first thing that happens when you hit send.

Your prompt doesn't enter the model as words — it gets chopped into chunks called *tokens*, which are then converted to numbers.

[KEY]A token is a chunk of text (a word, part of a word, or punctuation) that the model converts to a number before it can do anything with your prompt.[/KEY]

[EX]GPT-4's tokenizer has a vocabulary of about 100,000 tokens. A word like "running" might become one token; a rare word like "tokenization" might split into two or three pieces.[/EX]

[Q]
What does tokenization actually convert your words into?
A) A ranked list of possible meanings for each word
B) Numbers that the model can process mathematically
C) A compressed copy of the original sentence
ANS: B
[/Q]

replies.user: [CURRICULUM: Unit 1, Lesson 1] Teach me what physically happens inside an LLM when I type a prompt. Start with tokenization and next-token prediction. After explaining, give me a hands-on exercise.
replies.raw:
Here's something that might surprise you: the word "bank" is always the same token — whether you're talking about a riverbank or a savings account.

The model doesn't know which one you mean just from the word itself. Something else has to sort that out.

**Tokenization** is step one of everything. When you hit send, your message doesn't travel as words — it gets chopped into *tokens*, which are chunks of text (a word, part of a word, or punctuation). Each token gets converted to a number.

[EX]GPT-4's tokenizer has a vocabulary of about 100,000 tokens. "Unbelievable" might become three tokens: "un", "believ", "able" — each mapped to its own number.[/EX]

[KEY]Your prompt reaches the model as a sequence of numbers, not words.[/KEY]

[Q]
What does a tokenizer actually convert your words into?
A) A dictionary lookup of each word's definition
B) A sequence of numbers representing chunks of text
C) A compressed audio file the model can process
ANS: B
[/Q]
